findings.title: No independent verification that a runtime-supplied manifestSha256 matches the actual git-committed payment-operation-manifest.json
findings.counterexample: r15HostedComposition(pools, env, target, provider, manifestSha256) and dispatchR15Once only validate that manifestSha256 is a syntactically well-formed 64-hex string (packages/db/src/r15-operation-guard.ts:8) and that it matches whatever row was already installed in r15_activation.manifest. Unlike migrations, which have verifyR15MigrationSources() in scripts/hosted-payment-migrations.ts recomputing SHA-256 from the actual committed file and rejecting drift, there is no equivalent verifyR15OperationManifest() that recomputes the hash of docs/execution/p6/r15-evidence/payment-operation-manifest.json and compares it to the hash passed into the composition at call time. A future wiring change (e.g. a stale hash left over from a prior environment, a copy-paste from another manifest, or a caller reading the hash from the wrong evidence file) would be silently accepted as long as it happens to equal whatever hash the migration owner separately installed in the DB row, with no automated test catching source/DB divergence the way migration hash drift is caught today.
findings.impact: Low today: no call site in this diff invokes r15HostedComposition/dispatchR15Once with real data, and the DB-side reserve() still enforces the strict booking/attempt/merchant/location/amount match, so this is not currently exploitable. Before CreatePayment/GetPayment are actually wired to a live manifest, this is a defense-in-depth gap that could let a future integration bug silently target the wrong manifest hash without any test failing, unlike the migration-hash path which already has this protection.
findings.test_coverage: tests/unit/r15-operation-guard.test.ts and tests/readiness/r15-guard-postgres.ts exercise wrong-manifest rejection only against values supplied directly by the test itself; no test reads the actual (not-yet-existing) payment-operation-manifest.json and cross-checks its hash against a call site, because no such call site or file exists yet.
findings.minimum_safe_correction: Before wiring any live manifestSha256 value into r15HostedComposition/dispatchR15Once, add a verifyR15OperationManifest()-style function (mirroring verifyR15MigrationSources) that reads docs/execution/p6/r15-evidence/payment-operation-manifest.json from the committed source tree, recomputes its SHA-256, and throws on any mismatch with the hash actually used at the call site.
findings.required_proof: A test that tampers with the committed manifest JSON (or the hash argument) after installation and shows the new verification function rejects the mismatch before dispatchR15Once is ever invoked.

finding_dispositions.reason: The original finding's premise (a CreatePayment dispatcher with a duplicate-charge counterexample) was factually wrong, as the disposition concedes: r15-hosted-composition.ts and SquareSandboxPaymentTruth only ever perform GetPayment, and no CreatePayment call site exists in this diff. The real gap Codex found while investigating (a reconstructed r15HostedComposition instance could repeat the same GetPayment call across process restarts because providerInvoked/workerInvoked were plain in-memory booleans) is genuine and is now fixed: migration 0030 adds a singleton manifest + action-keyed operations table with a SECURITY DEFINER reserve() function; packages/db/src/r15-operation-guard.ts's dispatchR15Once() commits an irreversible row reservation (synchronous_commit=on) strictly BEFORE invoking send(), with send() deliberately outside the transaction so a crash before COMMIT never dispatches and any COMMIT ambiguity (response loss) is treated conservatively as consumed/blocked, never retried. This is exercised by real local PostgreSQL tests including a genuine forked child-process crash immediately after a successful reservation (tests/readiness/r15-guard-child.ts + r15-guard-postgres.ts), a commit-response-loss case, concurrent-reservation collapse to exactly one winner, and privilege tests showing no runtime role (including the worker role granted EXECUTE on reserve()) can read/rewrite the manifest or operations tables directly. tests/unit/r15-composition.test.ts's previously-failing 'reconstructed composition cannot repeat the same GetPayment after response loss' test (2 calls, f1-before.log) now passes (target.log) with only 1 lookup call. The worker-role-only grant, PUBLIC revocation, and fixed search_path on the SECURITY DEFINER function are all present and correctly scoped. CreatePayment itself remains entirely unwired to this guard (no call site, no test) — this is accurately described as a not-yet-activated prerequisite rather than a hidden fixed vulnerability, and is tracked in activation_prerequisites, not silently claimed as done.

tools/acceptance/r15-signature-handoff.ts now implements the previously-absent non-disclosing handoff: the key is sent to the Vercel CLI via stdin JSON only (never argv), the pipe subprocess (vercelSignatureKeySink) captures stdout in a bounded buffer and converts every failure into a fixed, cause-less error class, and handoffR15Signature's own catch swallows all underlying errors (including any that could carry the key) before rethrowing a fixed message. Returned success values contain only {state, projectId, keyName} — never the key. Subscription-context fields (enabled, api_version, notification_url, event_types, signature_key format) are validated before persistence is even attempted. tests/unit/r15-signature-handoff.test.ts covers success, throw, invalid-json, api-error, wrong-target, missing-receipt, and context-mismatch paths, all asserting the key never appears in the thrown error, its stack, or the returned value, plus a real child-process CLI pipe test for both success and failure. This matches the original required_proof (redacted-output test proving no return/log/exception path leaks the key). The actual live subscription-create -> handoff -> Vercel secret-store round trip remains unperformed, which is expected and correctly not claimed as done.

Nothing in this diff touches hosted Neon provisioning, migration application, or role creation; store_i5vh0ZEKo2ikcVo9 remains at 0 migrations/0 roles/0 connected projects with the 403 credential read unresolved, exactly as at the prior head. This finding cannot be resolved by any local code change, and the disposition correctly does not attempt to fake hosted evidence. The genuine conflict — Governance forbids new external writes until this review gate passes, while F3's own resolution requires an external write — is a sequencing question outside this reviewer's authority to resolve (I do not authorize hosted writes and do not instruct Codex to bypass the current no-write gate). Per governance's own severity rule, an unresolved original HIGH continues to block dependent live/external work; it is not downgraded, and the original HIGH remains in history regardless of this disposition. Resolution requires an explicit Owner/ChatGPT sequencing decision (see activation_prerequisites) — either a narrowly-scoped exception permitting migration/role work on the already-existing resource as a gate-supporting step, or formal deferral of F3's full resolution to the reserved final post-live review.
